facts.fact: The DHIS2 for Education country use case of October 2022 says the system was built together with the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education, starting with training at central level, with HISP WCA and the University of Oslo as partners.

The DHIS2 for Education country use case of October 2022 says the EMIS was aligned to the Education Policy 2016-2030 and its Monitoring and Evaluation Framework, moving from aggregate data to individual teacher and learner tracking.

The DHIS2 for Education country use case says a national student registration exercise in 2021 launched the individual student identification number, giving no count of schools and not saying who entered the records.

The DHIS2 for Education country use case of October 2022 says the implementation was then strengthening regional levels, and that training at district and community levels to make entry of school-level data possible was a final stage still to come; attendance apps were described as ongoing innovations.

systems.owner: Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education (MoBSE), with HISP WCA and the University of Oslo
systems.tiers: central level first, regional levels being strengthened in October 2022, district and community levels to follow

systems.system: Annual School Census and the annual statistical yearbook
systems.platform: paper questionnaire distributed to schools, manual data entry
systems.tiers: schools fill the form; highly centralised entry and aggregation

systems.owner: MoBSE, with HISP WCA and the University of Oslo

systems.system: Separate databases for HR, examinations and infrastructure
systems.tiers: fragmented, with no database bringing them together

note: The document describes the current EMIS in October 2022 as centralised, aggregated and paper-based on the Annual School Census, which is census. It does not say that schools keep learner records on paper, nor who entered the 2021 registration, so no kept or levels fact is taken.
